r.name: Beacon Way
r.operator: Walsall Council;Heart of England Way Assosciation
r.description: Starting at Sandwell Valley via the outskirts of Birmingham and the countryside of Walsall into Staffordshire. Take in the Forest of Mercia, lakes, nature reserves, woods, and canal banks. Named after Barr Beacon, one of the highest hills in this area.

r.name: North Birmingham Walking and Cycling Route
r.description: Route 535 is a small cycle route from National Cycle Route 5 in Birmingham City Centre to Gravelly Hill, which carries on for a short way along the Tame Valley Canal

r.name: Two Saints Way
r.description: Two Saints Way - Chester Cathedral to/from Lichfield Cathedral. In the late Middle Ages a steady stream of pilgrims walked this way – both housing shrines to two game-changing Mercian saints in the 7th century - St Werburgh and St Chad

r.name: The Way for the Millennium
r.description: Newport to Burton on Trent

r.name: Paupers Memorial Trail
r.description: Trail following history of Paupers in West Bromwich from the first dispensers of poor relief by monks at Sandwell Priory to the Poor Law Workhouse and burial site.

r.name: Rushall Junction to Ryders Green Locks
r.description: This route features an unusual aqueduct; one of the few examples of a canal crossing over a railway. Distance: 7.5 miles/12 km (approx) Duration: 1 hour 15 min (approx)

r.name: Dudley Port Circular
r.description: Follow The Gower Branch, then turn right back onto The Old Main Line. For a more challenging route, continue along The New Main Line and cross at Bromford Junction. Take the ramp access to The Old Main Line and double back, crossing Blakeley Hall Bridge.

r.name: West Bromwich to Oldbury Health Walk
r.description: Self-guided health walk through Black Country Millenium Urban Forest sites. Route passes 500+yr old Oak House and along the banks of the River Tame. Difficulty: Easy Duration: 45-60 mins

r.name: Galton Valley Health Walk
r.description: Self-guided health walk through Black Country Millenium Urban Forest sites. Route follows what was once the longest earthwork in the world and under Telford's Galton Bridge. Difficulty: Medium due to unsurfaced paths and steps Duration: 45-60 mins

r.name: Handsworth & Lozells Places of Worship Heritage Trail
r.description: Trail around Handsworth and Lozells- a culturally diverse area, where you can learn about the rich variety of religious communities who live alongside one another in a relatively small area.

r.name: Smethwick Places of Worship Heritage Trail
r.description: A trail around Smethwick- a culturally diverse area where you can learn about the wide variety of religious communities who live alongside one another in a relatively small area.

r.name: Birchfield Heritage Trail: Red Route
r.description: This trail reveals some of the hidden secrets Birchfield, how the place has changed and the many links between other parts of the world. The trail raises questions about Britain’s colonial history, the impacts of which continue today.

r.name: Birchfield Heritage Trail: Green Route
r.description: This trail reveals some of the hidden secrets Birchfield, how the place has changed and the many links between other parts of the world including the Commonwealth.

r.name: Handsworth Park Arts Trail
r.description: Handsworth Park Arts Trail is an exhibition of public art in the natural setting of one of Birmingham's most beautiful parks. Six new pieces are added to many other features in the Park.

r.name: 2km walk: Sutton Park
r.description: 2km circular walking trail around Sutton Park to/from the Visitor Centre. Marked by lime green footprints

r.name: 5km walk: Sutton Park
r.description: 5km circular walking trail around Sutton Park to/from the Visitor Centre. Marked by blue footprints

r.name: Sutton Park Archeology Walk 1: Streetly Gate
r.operator: Birmingham City Council;Friends of Sutton Park Association (FoSPA)
r.description: Most of Sutton Park is a Scheduled Ancient Monument and contains archaeological remains. This trail, one of six in the park, is via a roman road, medevial deer park, prehistoric mounds, medeval pond, and 16th century wood.

r.name: Sutton Park Archeology Walk 2: Town Gate
r.operator: Birmingham City Council;Friends of Sutton Park Association (FoSPA)
r.description: Most of Sutton Park is a Scheduled Ancient Monument and contains archaeological remains. This trail, one of six in the park, is via a medieval pond, medieval deer park, 16th-century wood, and 18th-century Mill Pond.

r.name: Sutton Park Archeology Walk 3: Banners Gate
r.operator: Birmingham City Council;Friends of Sutton Park Association (FoSPA)
r.description: Most of Sutton Park is a Scheduled Ancient Monument and contains archaeological remains. This trail, one of six in the park, is via a Roman road, medieval deer park, military target range, prehistoric burnt mound, and 18th-century Mill Pond.

r.name: Walsall Walk of Art
r.description: A specially designed circular canalside walk, starting from Walsall’s New Art Gallery, passing through changing landscapes. Distance: 4 miles/6.5 km(approx) Duration: 80 mins(approx)

r.name: Clayhanger Common Walk
r.description: Short, circular route following the Wyrley & Essington Canal to Clayhanger Common – one of Walsall’s much-loved areas of green, open space. Distance: 6 miles/9.5 km(approx) Duration: 120 mins(approx)

r.name: Four Commons Walk
r.description: Circular route following the Wyrley & Essington Canal to Clayhanger Common – one of Walsall’s much-loved areas of green, open space. Distance: 6 miles/9.5 km(approx) Duration: 120 mins(approx)

r.name: Sneyd Junction to Cannock Extension Canal
r.description: A semi-rural route following the curves of the canal, until it opens out into parkland at the Cannock Extension. Distance: 5.5 miles/8.8 km (approx) Duration: 45 min (approx)

r.name: Cannock Extension Canal to Longwood Junction
r.description: Canalside route leading past Clayhanger Common and through Rushall, with a pub along the way. Distance: 7 miles/11.2 km (approx) Duration: 60 min (approx)

r.name: Longwood Junction to Rushall Locks
r.description: A straight ride, beginning close to Hay Head Local Nature Reserve and continuing to the Rushall Lock Flight. Distance: 1.5 miles/2.4 km (approx) Duration: 60 min (approx)

r.name: Sneyd Junction to Pudding Green Junction
r.description: Canalside route passing through the heartlands of the industrial Black Country. Decends using the Walsall locks then rises at Ryders Green Locks. Distance: 10 miles/16 km (approx) Duration: 90 min (approx)

r.name: Factory Junction to Ladywood Junction
r.description: Cycle along The New Main Line and follow the signs for The National Cycle Route, which takes you to Ladywood Junction and on into Birmingham City Centre. Distance: 6 miles/10 km (approx) Duration: 60 min (approx)

r.name: Forest of Mercia Timberland Trail (Long Route)
r.operator: Timberland Clothing Company;The Countryside Agency;Walsall Metropolitan Borough Council
r.description: 10-mile circular route based on PRoW and canal towpaths, which would've been used by local miners, iron workers, and farmers. Car Parking at start on Wood Lane.

r.name: Forest of Mercia Timberland Trail (Short Route)
r.operator: Timberland Clothing Company;The Countryside Agency;Walsall Metropolitan Borough Council
r.description: 8-mile circular route based on PRoW and canal towpaths, which would've been used by local miners, iron workers, and farmers. Car Parking at the start on Wood Lane.

r.name: Walk Smethwick Heritage Trail
r.description: Heritage trail around Smethwick, once known as “the level land where cows graze” from Anglo-Saxon farms Canals fueled a boom, making steam engines, stained glass, ceramics & lighthouses. Historically known as “the workshop of the world.”

r.name: Sandwell Park Colliery Trail
r.description: The trail follows the remains of a tramway that was used to transport coal from the Sandwell Park Colliery Jubilee Pit to railway sidings and a canal wharf. It is now an area of natural beauty with plenty of wildlife, scenic views, and roaming livestock.
